clue.text: Apparatus for what batsmen and footballers do

definitions.meaning: a system of pulleys and rope for lifting heavy loads
a batsman stops the ball dead with his bat, a footballer wins the ball off an opponent

explanation.surface: A question about what piece of kit suits both cricketers and footballers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman 'blocks' a delivery by stopping it defensively; in football a player 'tackles' to win the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a rope-and-pulley hoist, and literally lists two sporting actions joined by 'and'.

clue.text: I am found in America under a part of the pitch for vegetables

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other, so it sits within it

parts.note: US is short for the United States
I in its object form is me

explanation.surface: A gardener describes vegetables grown in a corner of an American sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs; in a down clue 'under' puts the next piece below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils are pod-bearing plants eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Give authority to a county for furniture

parts.note: to chair a meeting is to preside over it with authority
Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Someone hands a county council the power to buy furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDS is the standard abbreviation of Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats that unfold into sleeping places are household fittings, a kind of furnishing.

clue.text: Look up in the district for a small space

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: an area is a district or region

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards turns the word round

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone looks up a small space in the local district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the little word for look in a down clue, and the result sits inside the district.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the term names a tiny interstice or ring-shaped gap in tissue.

clue.text: Is depressed when free rides are given around the resort

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are wrapped around another piece
free signals the letters are loosed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Free rides at a seaside resort somehow leave a visitor glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' scrambles the rides to DEIRS, which is split to go around the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose all hope is to be in low spirits, a synonym for being depressed.

clue.text: Pungent when caught in the dry

indicators.note: the letter is placed in the other word

parts.note: arid means dry
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A sharp smell catches someone in a dry place.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'caught' is a cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter, stinging smell or taste is sharp and pungent.

clue.text: Woman with a poem for negative terminal

parts.note: Kath is a woman's name
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A woman composes verse about an electrical part.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old spelling of the electrode usually written with C.
explanation.definitionFit: The electrode by which current leaves a device is its negative pole, an older spelling.

clue.text: Formerly steep about a sailor in an invigorating manner

parts.note: ex means former or formerly

indicators.note: one piece goes round the others

parts.note: hilly country is steep
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

explanation.surface: A former mountaineer describes a steep climb around a sailor as bracing.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a Royal Navy term for a sailor below officer rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something thrillingly and bracingly is doing it in an invigorating way.

clue.text: Surrender gravity in the enemy and die

parts.note: to give up is to surrender

indicators.note: the letter goes in the other words

parts.note: a host is an army, a hostile force
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A soldier surrenders gravely to the enemy and perishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' is the old sense of an army, here the enemy's forces.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for expiring or ceasing to function, equivalent to dying.

clue.text: Fashionable fireplace for unappreciative person

parts.note: in means fashionable
a grate is a fireplace

explanation.surface: A trendy fireplace is wasted on someone thankless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows no thanks for kindness is an ungrateful wretch.

clue.text: Period of time which makes a saint vomit

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint
to retch is to try to vomit

explanation.surface: A spell of time so dull it makes even a saint sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuous spell or term, including a prison term, is a span of time.

clue.text: Female made out of dear males

indicators.note: the letters are remade into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is fashioned out of beloved men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made out of' rearranges DEAR MALES.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, borne by the heroine of Hugo's Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Jester who makes his master look back and start laughing

indicators.note: his master looking backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lord is a master

indicators.note: the start of laughing gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A court fool makes his lord turn round and begin to giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look back' turns LORD into DROL; 'start' takes L from laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word once meant a buffoon or comic fool.

clue.text: Examination results one almost has to judge after a page

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the page letter
almost means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to assess is to judge

explanation.surface: A student almost has to rate a page of exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last S of ASSESS, leaving ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Successful outcomes in exams are graded as such.

clue.text: George and Elizabeth without a universal majesty

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so these letters go round another

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: King George and Queen Elizabeth lack universal majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: ER goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour and stateliness are what majesty conveys.

clue.text: Behold the essence behind one changing into a coiner

indicators.note: the following pieces come behind the shuffled word
the letters of the word change into a new order

parts.note: lo means behold
the gist is the essence

explanation.surface: Someone sees the essence of a person changing into a forger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges ONE into NEO; LO and GIST come 'behind' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who invents new words is a coiner of terms, not of counterfeit money.

clue.text: Rate vice possibly responsive to stimulus

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could form another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grading vice might show how sensitive someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RATE VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacting readily to a prompt means being quick to respond to stimulus.

clue.text: Rushed round an animal and caused confusion

indicators.note: one word goes round the other

parts.note: hared means rushed
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone rushed around a donkey and stirred up chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester and fluster someone is to trouble and confuse them.

clue.text: One is held by a Glasgow person to be taller and thinner

indicators.note: the letter is held by the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a Ranger is a player or fan of Rangers, a Glasgow football club
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian holds one man up as tall and lanky.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Glasgow football club; 'is held by' puts I inside RANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-limbed and lean describes someone tall and slender.

clue.text: Man is in the right month for what a bishop wears

indicators.note: one piece is in the other

parts.note: Oct is short for October
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man in the right month dresses as a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A white linen vestment like a surplice is worn by bishops.

clue.text: Nelson is hot on speech

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece rests on the other

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
oratio is the Latin word for speech

explanation.surface: Nelson is said to be fiery on oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Lord Nelson's first name; the speech is the Latin word, without the English final N.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the British admiral Nelson, victor at Trafalgar.

clue.text: Apparatuses which have an island at heart

definitions.text: Apparatuses which have an island at heart

parts.words: Apparatuses which have an island at heart
parts.note: diving breathing sets whose name has a Caribbean island in its middle

explanation.surface: Equipment with an island at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Caribbean island CUBA sits in the middle of the word, flanked by S on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwater breathing sets are diving apparatuses, and their name has the island of Cuba at its centre.

clue.text: Furry creature appearing in huge nettles

indicators.note: the letters appear inside the following words

explanation.surface: An animal turns up in a patch of huge nettles.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spotted cat-like carnivore with soft fur.

clue.text: They obstruct the hearing for part of the period which holds a student activity

indicators.note: the trimmed word holds the other inside
only part of the word is used, losing its end

parts.note: time is a period
rag is a British student charity event

explanation.surface: Something blocking hearing during a student event.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British university fund-raising festival; 'part of' trims TIME to TI, which holds RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: These small flaps of cartilage project in front of the ear canal, partly covering it.

clue.text: Apparatus which is a little bit backward in what is nearly a storm

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other
nearly means the word is cut short by a letter

parts.note: a cyclone is a storm

indicators.note: backward reads the word in reverse

parts.note: an ort is a scrap or small leftover bit

explanation.surface: A machine somehow slightly behind in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts CYCLONE to CYCLON; 'backward' turns ORT to TRO, put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle accelerator is a scientific machine.

clue.text: Japanese art addressed to city on the motorway

parts.note: O is the vocative exclamation used when addressing someone
Riga is the capital of Latvia
M1 is a British motorway, read as MI

explanation.surface: A Japanese art greets a city on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of paper folding is a traditional art form.

clue.text: City which is sometimes ahead of fashion

definitions.meaning: a port city in south-west England
the city's name precedes fashion in the phrase shipshape and ... fashion

explanation.surface: A city sometimes leads the trends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipshape and Bristol fashion' is a British phrase meaning neat and in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: A major English port city, and the word placed before fashion in a nautical idiom.

clue.text: Apostasy which is an unusual sovereign trait

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters are in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Renouncing a faith is an odd quality for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges SOVEREIGN TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning one's back on a faith or cause, desertion of principle.
